verdict: A tough week: both ad channels went dark and lead volume dropped sharply.
narrative: Over the past 28 days you received 117 leads at a cost of $16.77 each, all sourced from Meta — Google spent $457.72 and delivered zero leads. This past week was particularly difficult: both Meta and Google ran at $0 spend for three consecutive days (September 17–19), which drove a 58% drop in leads week-over-week and pushed cost per lead up 34% in that window. The three dark days are the primary cause of the dip, not a change in underlying efficiency. Ads are back in motion and several overdue build milestones — including paid landing pages, updated creative, and CRM configuration — are being resolved this period so the funnel can operate without interruption. Once those pieces are confirmed live, you should see lead volume stabilize and cost per lead settle back toward the mid-period average.

highlights.phrase: leads received this 28-day period, all from Meta
average cost per lead this period, up 34% in the last week due to three dark-spend days
opportunities created in your CRM this period — none yet progressed to appointment or close, which is being addressed

watch_item.issue: 151 leads entered your CRM over 28 days but zero progressed to an appointment or a won opportunity, pointing to a gap in intake or follow-up.
watch_item.fix: CRM workflow and follow-up sequencing are being audited and closed out as part of the current build milestone, with completion targeted by end of September.
